summary: M104 is the accepted implementation baseline: LangGraph local runtime, SQLite checkpoint, interrupt/resume, repair loop, subgraph/supervisor probe, stream evidence, Studio graph configuration, and Cocos graph pressure test are integrated. M105-M108 now focus on Cocos real-project quality and player-view validation while preserving workflow receipt, lease, write_set, provider live proof, evidence, and operator packet rules.

repaid_items.description: Orchestrator/CLI/Web/chat surfaces concentrated too much behavior in large facade files.
repaid_items.result: Facade ratchets, interaction split, chat runtime package, CLI command families, and Web UI split landed.

repaid_items.description: scheduler-authority naming could overstate consensus guarantees beyond local lease semantics.
repaid_items.result: Default semantics now use LocalSchedulerLeaseArbiter; scheduler-authority names are legacy compatibility or explicit cluster-on surfaces.

repaid_items.description: capability health relied too much on descriptor readiness instead of runtime probe evidence.
repaid_items.result: CapabilityProbeResult, runtime ledger evidence, API/CLI health projection, and require-live probes were added.
Added scope_hash and scope_payload, and rejected legacy high-risk receipts without scope binding.

repaid_items.description: Capability probes could accept simulated, dry-run, generic, or fallback-only evidence.
repaid_items.result: Provider-specific live-proof contracts now reject false-positive readiness evidence.
Added quick/full/shard entrypoints, timeout traces, and last-command evidence.

repaid_items.description: Operator Web UI still depended on inline CSP exceptions and unsafe browser-surface paths.
repaid_items.result: Moved operator CSS/JS to static assets, removed unsafe-inline, and replaced unsafe innerHTML paths.

repaid_items.description: MCP include_mcp behavior could expose too broad a profile set.
repaid_items.result: Added canonical tool id, selector, and collision guard semantics.

repaid_items.description: Pipeline lacked a formal product-layer contract.
Pipeline lacked a minimum execution entrypoint.
repaid_items.result: Added serial workflowctl pipeline run with stage evidence and short-circuit semantics.

repaid_items.description: OpenAI API, Codex CLI, MiniMax/DeepSeek API, OpenCode CLI, MMX/GCP/Vertex generation, MCP tools, and LangChain were too easy to conflate.
repaid_items.result: Provider contracts, verified-only capability health, provider alias live-proof aggregation, and route stats separate API, CLI, MCP, asset generation, and experimental agent surfaces.

repaid_items.description: MMX/MiniMax was primarily wired as text evidence rather than true image, speech, and music generation.
repaid_items.result: MiniMax image/speech/music wrappers, binary live proof, Cocos asset manifest, reusable asset factory, hash dedupe, retry, and required-asset NO-GO gates are implemented.

repaid_items.description: Vertex, gcloud, and GCP TTS boundaries were unclear.
repaid_items.result: GCP TTS is split as gcp_tts_api; Vertex Imagen and Gemini visual-review wrappers/probes are live and consumed by asset factory QA.

repaid_items.description: Pipeline run needed proof that stages truly execute, short-circuit on failure, and write evidence.
repaid_items.result: commercial_cocos_game template executes asset factory, Cocos generation/build/playtest, readiness gate, and writes stage evidence.

repaid_items.description: Active docs could describe completed work as planned/current/open.
repaid_items.result: Added workflowctl governance active-truth-check and stale truth checks.

repaid_items.description: Cocos, asset generation, asset factory, and business pipeline template code entered packages/core_domain, weakening the boundary between workflow control-plane code and vertical business production code.
repaid_items.introduced_in: M77-M83 commercial Cocos and asset pipeline work
repaid_items.result: Moved vertical asset/Cocos implementations to packages/contributions, removed expired core_domain compatibility shims, and routed core callers through runtime_integrations adapters.

repaid_items.description: Pipeline execution semantics could overstate truth: placeholders were completed, skipped dependencies could satisfy downstream stages, validation commands used shell execution, and commercial gates could miss player-visible commercial_playable_go.
repaid_items.result: Stage placeholders are stubbed/blocked, required dependencies need completed status, validation uses the safe command runner, and commercial gates bind --require-commercial to commercial_playable_go.

repaid_items.description: The project lacked production/core/file ratchets that prevent unchecked growth while preserving necessary test growth.
repaid_items.result: Added core_domain purity, production LOC, business file size, and architecture-doc tests, with M88/M90 growth explicitly ratcheted.

repaid_items.description: Workflow had custom orchestration, checkpoint, review gate, resume, parallelism, and repair-loop behavior that overlapped with LangGraph primitives.
repaid_items.result: Established the boundary where LangGraph carries graph state, checkpoint, interrupt/resume, subgraph/supervisor probes, repair loops, stream evidence, and Cocos graph pressure execution while workflow keeps receipts, leases, write_set audit, provider live proof, evidence, and operator packets.

open_items.description: Cocos game pipeline can generate, build, playtest, and package a project, but the generated result is not yet commercial-playable: UI is primitive, panels are shallow, level switching is mostly state mutation, audio/voice design is poor, and double-click HTML launch is unsupported.
open_items.blocking_impact: Blocks claiming final commercial game readiness; does not block preserving and improving the commercial game pipeline.

open_items.description: Commercial readiness tests rely too much on internal E2E state flags and not enough on player-visible UI, usable panels, gameplay depth, audio experience, and mobile visual quality.
open_items.blocking_impact: Blocks future GO decisions for commercial game generation until the gate distinguishes technical smoke, production scaffold, and commercial-playable output.

open_items.description: LangChain remains present as an agent adapter but does not currently provide a mainline capability that direct APIs, MCP broker, or CLI agents cannot cover.
repositories.py, service_lifecycle.py, service_projection.py, interaction_catalog.py, and models.py remain large.
open_items.blocking_impact: Non-blocking maintainability debt; revisit when capability development exposes real friction.

freeze_review_questions: Did the active phase use multiple task cards, or explicitly mark a justified single_card_exception?
Did the phase run workflow route previews and preserve task-card/evidence/operator-packet proof?
Do all high-risk receipt/lease paths bind the consumed authorization to the actual request scope?
Do all capability providers pass provider-specific live-proof contracts without simulated, dry-run, generic, or fallback-only evidence?
Do active docs avoid claiming zero debt, scheduler consensus, automatic PR publication, Gemini CLI support, or provider readiness beyond verified runtime facts?
Does workflowctl governance self-development-manifest remain GO before declaring a milestone ready for capability-layer work?
Does the active development plan stop at milestone/phase level and defer task-card generation until a phase is active?
Does packages/core_domain remain free of new Cocos/H5/game executor, commercial asset generator, business pipeline template, and vertical QA/playtest modules?
Do pipeline stage results distinguish completed, blocked, failed, skipped, stubbed, and simulated without marking unexecuted work completed?
Do validation commands use packages/runtime_security/safe_command_runner.py with shell metacharacter rejection and shell=False by default?
Do active game-pipeline docs and gates distinguish technical smoke, E2E scaffold success, production scaffold success, and final commercial-playable readiness?
Does any new graph-backed execution keep receipt, lease, workspace root, write_set, provider live proof, and evidence/operator packet semantics outside LangGraph shortcuts?
